Can we get here? Isn't the callback set in the constructor?
Yes because the caller can pass in a nullptr as well, also will run into clang errors if we don't check this.
spelling: as->has
this is expected to be as "as" it states the reason for skip.

You aren't using `addressRanges` variable
Wouldn't the linter catch that?
Done
Why are you passing the reference to the unique pointer? You should be able to pass a reference without the smart pointer
Done
Will this eventually move to configuration? Can we put a TODO for that?
No, this will continue to be here. The configuration will define this as a string.

2 things:
1) Can you put a comment that this is doing ascii decoding?
2) I think you need to break when you hit `\0` or -`\0`. We do similar stuff in: https://github.com/facebook/openbmc/blob/helium/common/recipes-core/rackmon2/rackmon/Register.cpp#L29-L35

> 2 things:
> 1) Can you put a comment that this is doing ascii decoding?

Done added a comment.

> 2) I think you need to break when you hit `\0` or -`\0`. We do similar stuff in: https://github.com/facebook/openbmc/blob/helium/common/recipes-core/rackmon2/rackmon/Register.cpp#L29-L35

This is implicitly taken care by this code so we don't have to do it explicitly. I have also added the Model test case around similar test data, so it verifies this works.
This might be a premature optimization but why do you create a string value for registers you don't care about? Can you do the string creation in fillInventorySourceProperties when you need it?

I am only creating the string value for registers which are part of config and passing it to fillInventorySourceProperties to set it. The config will only have the registers as mentioned in fillInventorySourceProperties not more than that. So, no extra work is being done.
Is the expectation that all registers are strings? If not, how will the type be distinguished?
Yes, all inventory registers are strings.
Can we use a type here that has an explicit `start` and `end`
Done
